style.vernacular: Coral-limestone island with a British colonial legacy: Georgian and Jacobean-influenced plantation houses and churches in plastered coral stone, Victorian Gothic civic buildings in Bridgetown, and a vast stock of timber chattel houses painted in bright pastels and saturated colours with white trim and steep gabled roofs of galvanised sheet or timber shingle. Modern building is rendered concrete block with flat or shallow-pitched roofs, jalousie windows and hurricane shutters, set among palms, mahogany, casuarina and bougainvillea.
style.ornament: Gingerbread fretwork and jigsaw trim on chattel-house eaves and verandas; louvred jalousie windows and hurricane shutters; coral-stone quoins and shaped Jacobean gables on great houses; pitched roofs with dormers (Demerara windows); Victorian Gothic pointed windows and clock tower on Parliament; white trim picking out brightly painted walls.

sources.what: chattel houses are small timber gabled houses in bright colours on coral-block supports; Georgian plantation houses in plastered coral stone with verandas; coral stone is the local material
early churches built from coral and limestone, the island's non-volcanic stone
